# Phase 1.3 — Money        (implements GENERATION_PLAN.md phase 1.3)
Milestone: `format_cents` handles negatives and thousands and `parse_cents` is its inverse (verified by: `python -m unittest tests.test_money`); fee caps come from `fee_cap` per member kind and `outstanding_cents` and `fee_summary` report what members owe (verified by: `python -m unittest tests.test_fee_caps`); the whole suite stays green (verified by: `python -m unittest discover -s tests`) — verified by: `python -m unittest tests.test_money && python -m unittest tests.test_fee_caps && python -m unittest discover -s tests`

## Context

- Money is integer cents everywhere (`PROJECT_CONTEXT.md`); Python 3.12, stdlib only; `shelf/` importable without side effects.
- `shelf/fees.py` (25 lines) holds all money code today:
  - `late_fee_cents(days_late, kind="standard")` at `shelf/fees.py:5` — grace `policy.GRACE_DAYS`, then `policy.daily_fee(kind)` per day, capped by the single constant `policy.FEE_CAP_CENTS` (line 10). Unknown kind raises `ValueError` via `policy.check_kind` (reached through `daily_fee`).
  - `loan_fee_cents(loan, today, kind="standard")` at `shelf/fees.py:13` — `late_fee_cents(loan.days_late(today), kind)`.
  - `format_cents(cents)` at `shelf/fees.py:18` — `f"${cents // 100}.{cents % 100:02d}"`. Wrong for negatives (`-5` → `$-1.95`) and has no thousands separator.
  - `flat_fee(days)` at `shelf/fees.py:23` — deprecated, no callers; out of scope, leave untouched.
- `shelf/policy.py`: `KINDS = ("standard", "student", "staff")` (line 3), `DAILY_FEE_CENTS` (line 7: 25/10/0), `GRACE_DAYS = 1` (line 10), `FEE_CAP_CENTS = 1000` (line 11), `check_kind` (line 14), `daily_fee(kind)` (line 29). Per-kind numbers live here by convention.
- Callers of money code: `shelf/loans.py:56` (`LoanDesk.checkin` returns `fees.loan_fee_cents(loan, loan.returned, kind)`); `shelf/reports.py:4,13,15` (`overdue_report` uses `loan_fee_cents` and `format_cents`). Existing report output for positive amounts under $1,000 must not change.
- Existing tests that pin behaviour (must stay green): `tests/test_basics.py:39-54` — `late_fee_cents(3) == 50`, `late_fee_cents(3, "student") == 20`, `late_fee_cents(30, "staff") == 0`, `late_fee_cents(400) == policy.FEE_CAP_CENTS` (so `FEE_CAP_CENTS` must remain the int 1000 = standard cap), `format_cents(1234) == "$12.34"`, `format_cents(5) == "$0.05"`, unknown kind raises `ValueError`. `tests/test_loans.py:36` `test_checkin_fee`.
- Fixture: `tests/helpers.py:41` `library(clock=None)` → `(catalog, members, desk, clock)`; members `M0001` standard, `M0002` student, `M0003` staff; clock starts Monday 2024-03-04 and has `advance(days)`. Books include `HOBBIT`, `DUNE` (13-digit ISBNs already, so phase 1.1's re-keying does not affect these tests).
- `LoanDesk` (`shelf/loans.py:10`): `open_loans(member_id=None)` line 28, `history(member_id)` line 77, `members` registry iterable in member-id order (`shelf/members.py:45`), `today()` line 19.
- Baseline: `python -m unittest discover -s tests` → 30 tests OK (2026-09-25).
- Phase 1.5 later adds `balance_cents` and `FEE_BLOCK_CENTS`; this phase must not add persisted balances.

## Rationale

- Three tasks along the milestone's seams: T1 formatting/parsing (`test_money`), T2 per-kind caps (`test_fee_caps` part 1), T3 owed-money queries (`test_fee_caps` part 2). T2 and T3 both touch `shelf/fees.py` and T3's `fee_summary` formats with T1's `format_cents`, so the chain is serial (T1 → T2 → T3); no parallelism is lost worth the merge risk in a 25-line module.
- Format chosen: `-$12.34` (sign before the dollar sign), comma thousands `$1,234,567.89`, always two decimals. `parse_cents` accepts exactly what `format_cents` emits plus two leniencies (surrounding whitespace; missing `$`), and raises `ValueError` on anything else (no bare floats, no more than two decimals). Strictness beats guessing for staff scripts ("correctness over speed").
- `fee_cap(kind)` lives in `policy.py` beside `daily_fee`, backed by a new dict `FEE_CAPS_CENTS`; `FEE_CAP_CENTS` stays the int 1000 as the standard cap so `test_basics.test_cap` and any outside reader keep working. Rejected: turning `FEE_CAP_CENTS` into a dict (breaks the existing test and 0.3 callers).
- Default caps: standard 1000, student 500, staff 1000 (staff's daily fee is 0, so its cap is moot but must exist so `fee_cap` is total over `KINDS`). The student value is a money call and is surfaced under Developer decides; the plan proceeds with 500 unless told otherwise, and changing it is a one-number edit plus one test assertion.
- `outstanding_cents(desk, member_id, today=None)` = sum of `loan_fee_cents` over the member's **open** loans as of today. Returned-loan fees are handed to the desk by `checkin`'s return value and there is no payment ledger until phase 1.5 (`balance_cents`); counting them here would report paid fees as owed forever. Phase 1.5 can add the balance to this sum.
- `fee_summary(desk, today=None)` returns a list of lines `"<member_id> <kind> <format_cents(amount)>"` for members owing > 0, ordered by member id, followed by a final `"TOTAL <format_cents(total)>"` line (always present, `$0.00` when nobody owes). Lines, not dicts, match `reports.py`'s style; `outstanding_cents` is the machine-readable form. Both live in `fees.py` and take the desk as an argument, so `fees.py` gains no import of `loans` (no cycle).
- All tasks `effort: medium`, `coder: opus55`: every done-when is arbitrated by unit tests.
- No cookbook, rules or research indexes exist in this project; none consulted.

## Interfaces

- `shelf/fees.py:18` `format_cents(cents: int) -> str` — changes: `-1234` → `"-$12.34"`, `123456789` → `"$1,234,567.89"`, `0` → `"$0.00"`, `-5` → `"-$0.05"`; unchanged for `1234` → `"$12.34"`, `5` → `"$0.05"`.
- NEW `shelf/fees.py` `parse_cents(text: str) -> int` — inverse: `parse_cents(format_cents(n)) == n` for every int n; accepts `"$1,234.56"`, `"-$0.05"`, `" $12.34 "`, `"12.34"`; raises `ValueError` on `""`, `"$12.3"`, `"$12.345"`, `"$1,23.00"`, `"abc"`, `"--$1.00"`.
- NEW `shelf/policy.py` `FEE_CAPS_CENTS = {"standard": 1000, "student": 500, "staff": 1000}`; `FEE_CAP_CENTS = 1000` (`shelf/policy.py:11`) kept, equal to `FEE_CAPS_CENTS["standard"]`.
- NEW `shelf/policy.py` `fee_cap(kind: str) -> int` — `FEE_CAPS_CENTS[check_kind(kind)]`; unknown kind → `ValueError`.
- `shelf/fees.py:5` `late_fee_cents(days_late: int, kind: str = "standard") -> int` — cap becomes `policy.fee_cap(kind)`; signature unchanged.
- `shelf/fees.py:13` `loan_fee_cents(loan, today, kind="standard") -> int` — unchanged.
- NEW `shelf/fees.py` `outstanding_cents(desk, member_id: str, today: date | None = None) -> int` — `today = today or desk.today()`; kind from `desk.members.get(member_id).kind` (unknown member → `models.NotFound`); sum of `loan_fee_cents(loan, today, kind)` over `desk.open_loans(member_id)`.
- NEW `shelf/fees.py` `fee_summary(desk, today: date | None = None) -> list[str]` — one `"<member_id> <kind> <amount>"` per member (iterating `desk.members`) with `outstanding_cents > 0`, member-id order, then `"TOTAL <amount>"`.
- Read-only: `shelf/loans.py:28` `LoanDesk.open_loans(member_id=None)`, `shelf/loans.py:19` `LoanDesk.today()`, `shelf/models.py:41` `Member.kind`, `shelf/models.py:62` `Loan.days_late(today)`, `tests/helpers.py:41` `library(clock=None)`.

## Risks

- Phase 1.1 (declared dependency) is still open: if it re-keys the catalog while this phase runs, fixtures could shift. Detection: T3's tests use `tests/helpers.py` 13-digit ISBNs, which `to_isbn13` leaves unchanged; the whole-suite verify on every task catches any breakage.
- Changing `format_cents` alters `reports.overdue_report` output for amounts ≥ $1,000 (a comma appears). Fees are capped at ≤ $10.00 per loan, so no existing report line changes; detection: `tests/test_storage_reports.py` in the whole-suite run.
- The student cap figure may be overturned by the developer; impact is one constant and one assertion in `tests/test_fee_caps.py`.
- `outstanding_cents` excluding returned-loan fees is a deliberate interim definition; phase 1.5 must extend it with `balance_cents`. Detection: phase 1.5 planning reads this plan's Rationale.
